## The Election Result

The final count from 13 September 2026. These figures are settled.

| Party | Vote share | Seats |
|-------|-----------|-------|
| Socialdemokraterna (S) | 31.6% | 110 |
| Sverigedemokraterna (SD) | 20.3% | 71 |
| Moderaterna (M) | 19.7% | 69 |
| Miljöpartiet (MP) | 8.5% | 29 |
| Centerpartiet (C) | 6.2% | 22 |
| Kristdemokraterna (KD) | 5.0% | 17 |
| Liberalerna (L) | 4.5% | 16 |
| Vänsterpartiet (V) | 4.3% | 15 |

Parties in the chamber: S, SD, M, MP, C, KD, L, V.

**The Liberals ARE in the chamber.** They cleared the four-percent threshold with 4.5% and hold 16 seats. They vote, they count toward the 175 needed to block a government, and they can be given cabinet posts. Any narrative describing them as outside parliament, as lacking representation, or as commentators without votes is wrong.

Left bloc (S, V, MP): **154** seats. Right bloc (M, SD, KD, L): **173** seats. The Centre Party holds **22** and sits with neither.

An absolute majority is 175 of 349. The left bloc is 21 short of one. The right bloc is 2 short of one.

## What the Night Meant for Each Party

Change against 2022, which is what each party will weigh when judging whether an extraordinary election would help or hurt it. Note that an extra election does not start a new four-year term: those elected serve only until the next ordinary election, so even a party riding high wins a shortened mandate.

| Party | Seats | 2022 | Change |
|-------|-------|------|--------|
| S | 110 | 107 | +3 |
| SD | 71 | 73 | -2 |
| M | 69 | 68 | +1 |
| MP | 29 | 18 | +11 |
| C | 22 | 24 | -2 |
| KD | 17 | 19 | -2 |
| L | 16 | 16 | ±0 |
| V | 15 | 24 | -9 |

## What Was Said Before the Vote

- The Centre Party repeated throughout the campaign that it will not seek organised cooperation with the Sweden Democrats, and will not support any government containing the Left Party.
- The Social Democrats ruled out cooperation with the Sweden Democrats, and declined to name any constellation they would pursue.
- The Sweden Democrats finished ahead of the Moderates and spent the closing week saying plainly that the largest party on the right expects cabinet seats this time. That demand is now on the record.
- The Liberals cleared the threshold against expectations, and are openly crediting tactical vote-lending from Moderate voters. They argue that they earned their place by making the last government work, and have restated their resistance to Sweden Democrat cabinet seats.
